summary:
CropShift AI is an Earth observation powered deep learning system designed for intelligent crop rotation and climate resilient farming, demonstrated in Sindh, Pakistan. The project integrates high resolution Copernicus Sentinel-2: ESA data, NASA POWER agroclimatology datasets, and Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) soil moisture metrics into a modular pipeline featuring SegFormer, ConvLSTM, and XGBoost models.
Unlike traditional tools that only monitor current crop health, CropShift AI addresses agricultural climate challenges by evaluating alternative crop rotation strategies, such as introducing nitrogen fixing legumes or drought resilient crops against seasonal water requirements, soil health impacts, and economic priorities.
This system is vital because it delivers explainable, transparent agronomic insights rather than simple heatmaps, empowering smallholder farmers to optimize constrained water resources, mitigate extreme thermal stress, and reverse soil degradation for sustainable long-term productivity.
details:
Project Overview & Functionality

CropShift AI is an Earth observation powered decision support system designed specifically for smallholder farmers in the climate vulnerable Hyderabad and Jamshoro agricultural belt of Sindh, Pakistan. The platform addresses severe regional challenges such as extreme summer temperatures exceeding 39°C, canal water rationing, and continuous cotton monoculture that depletes soil nitrogen by providing actionable, climate resilient crop rotation recommendations.

The system works by ingesting multi-source geospatial and meteorological telemetry:

  • Satellite Observations: Utilizes 30 meter Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery via NASA Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) products (HLSS30) to compute key vegetative and water indices, specifically Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI):
  • Agroclimatology & Soil Context: Integrates daily meteorological variables (temperature, precipitation) from NASA POWER and root-zone soil moisture context from SMAP (~9 km grid context).
  • AI & Machine Learning Core:
  • SegFormer for 30m spatial crop and vegetation segmentation.
  • ConvLSTM for spatiotemporal seasonal stress analysis.
  • XGBoost for multi-objective rotation suitability scoring.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Climate Resilience: Shifts smallholder agriculture from reactive crisis management to proactive, data-driven planning by anticipating thermal and water stress.
  • Resource Optimization: Optimizes constrained irrigation schedules and canal water availability.
  • Soil Restoration: Reverses nitrogen depletion caused by continuous monoculture by intelligently recommending nitrogen-fixing rotation crops (e.g., mung beans) alongside staple crops like wheat and cotton.
  • Economic Stability: Maximizes farm profitability and long-term yield sustainability across Sindh's farming communities.

Tech Stack, Tools & Software

  • Programming Language: Python 3.10+
  • Deep Learning & Machine Learning: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers (SegFormer), TensorFlow/Keras (ConvLSTM), XGBoost, Scikit-Learn.
  • Geospatial & Data Processing: Rasterio, NumPy, Pandas, NASA POWER API.
  • Application Framework & Deployment: Streamlit dashboard running interactively via Google Colab with secure tunneling (pyngrok).

Creativity & Design Considerations

  • Hyper-Localized Focus: Tailored precisely to the agro-ecological realities of the Sindh region (Hyderabad/Jamshoro), accounting for local canal irrigation cycles and extreme heat thresholds.
  • Explainable AI (XAI): Rather than acting as a black-box model, CropShift AI provides transparent agronomic reasoning, risk profiles, and trade-off metrics (water demand vs. soil recovery) for every rotation suggestion.
  • Accessibility: Designed to run seamlessly in zero-install cloud environments (Google Colab) with a user-friendly Streamlit interface, ensuring that researchers, extension workers, and agricultural stakeholders can easily deploy and interact with the model worldwide.
